weeks.title: Understanding Content Strategy
weeks.overview:
Welcome back to UCA.

By now, you have started building your personal brand and publishing content on your social media account. You have begun exploring what you want to be known for, who you want to reach, and the kind of content you can create.

Now, it is time to become more intentional about what you publish.

Posting consistently is important, but consistency alone is not enough. You also need to understand what to post, why you are posting it, who it is meant for, and how your content contributes to your personal brand.

This is where content strategy comes in.

Over these two days, you will learn how to approach content creation more strategically, generate content ideas, and develop a simple system for planning and publishing your content.

The goal is not to make you a content strategist overnight. It is to help you move beyond posting randomly and begin creating content with purpose.

lessons.title: What You'll Learn — Across Monday and Tuesday
lessons.content:
ACROSS MONDAY AND TUESDAY, YOU WILL EXPLORE THREE KEY AREAS:

1. Understanding Content Strategy
2. Content Ideation
3. Content Systems

These three areas work together.

Content strategy gives your content direction, content ideation helps you discover what to create, and content systems help you organise your ideas and publish consistently.

lessons.title: Part 1 — Understanding Content Strategy
lessons.content:
Content strategy is the process of deciding what content you will create, who it is for, why you are creating it, and how it supports your goals.

Instead of waking up every day wondering what to post, you begin to understand the purpose behind your content and the role each post plays in building your personal brand.

In this lesson, you will be introduced to content pillars and content buckets, which help you organise the subjects and formats you regularly create.

You will also explore different types of content, including educational, entertaining, inspirational, storytelling, personal, promotional, opinion-based, and authority-building content.

Understanding these categories will help you recognise the different ways you can communicate with your audience without making every post feel the same.

Your content should not simply exist to fill your page. It should help people understand your interests, learn from you, connect with your perspective, appreciate your work, or take an appropriate next step.

WATCH THE LESSON

Understanding Content Strategy
https://youtu.be/H9DXLvR-Yb8

Watch the full lesson and begin thinking about the main subjects you want your personal brand to be associated with.

lessons.title: Part 2 — Content Ideation
lessons.content:
One of the biggest challenges in content creation is figuring out what to post.

You may have the skills, knowledge, and desire to build your personal brand, but without a reliable way to generate ideas, you can quickly run out of things to say.

Content ideation is the process of discovering, developing, and organising ideas that can be turned into useful or interesting content.

In this lesson, you will explore different sources of content ideas, including audience questions, common problems, personal experiences, trends, comments, competitors, search results, news, personal stories, industry developments, and frequently asked questions.

You will begin to understand that content ideas are not limited to waiting for inspiration. They can be discovered by paying attention to the questions people ask, the problems they experience, the conversations happening in your industry, and the lessons you encounter in your own journey.

For example, as a Video Editor, you could create content about common editing mistakes, lessons from a recent project, or a technique you have just learned.

As a Graphic Designer, you could discuss design principles, explain a design decision, or share the process behind a project.

As a Content Writer, you could explore writing mistakes, share useful writing lessons, or respond to common questions about writing.

The goal is to develop the habit of noticing ideas and turning them into content that serves your audience and supports your personal brand.

WATCH THE LESSON

Content Ideation
https://youtu.be/h_yQswsXwhY

Watch the full lesson and pay attention to how you can generate ideas from your everyday experiences, your audience, and your chosen field.

lessons.title: Part 3 — Building Your Content System
lessons.content:
Having good content ideas is important, but ideas alone will not guarantee consistent publishing.

You also need a simple system for organising those ideas, planning your content, and making time to create it.

A content system helps you move from deciding what to post to actually preparing and publishing your posts.

In this lesson, you will explore content calendars, weekly planning, content batching, recurring series, repeatable formats, evergreen content, and trending content.

You will learn why planning ahead can reduce the pressure of having to invent a new idea every day. You will also begin to understand how recurring formats and content series can make content creation easier over time.

Evergreen content can remain useful for a long time, while trending content allows you to respond to relevant conversations and developments happening now.

You do not need an elaborate content management system at this stage. A simple calendar, a collection of organised ideas, and a realistic publishing plan can provide a strong starting point.

The objective is to create a process you can maintain alongside your other UCA learning activities.

WATCH THE LESSON

Content Systems
https://youtu.be/4C3MH0A2Sn8

Watch the full lesson and think about how you can organise your ideas and establish a practical content creation routine.

lessons.title: Your Task
lessons.content:
After completing the three lessons, begin applying what you have learned to your own personal brand.

Complete the following:

- Identify three to five content pillars that align with your personal brand and interests.
- Brainstorm at least 15 content ideas using different sources of inspiration.
- Identify different content types you can use to communicate with your audience.
- Organise your ideas into a simple content bank.
- Create a basic content calendar for the coming week.
- Decide when you will create, prepare, and publish your content.
- Continue publishing on your personal-brand account.

Remember, your content plan does not have to be perfect. It should be simple enough for you to use consistently and flexible enough to improve as you learn.

lessons.title: Today's Goal
lessons.content:
The goal of these two sessions is to help you move from posting without a clear plan to creating content with greater intention.

By the end of Monday and Tuesday, you should understand the basics of content strategy, know how to generate content ideas from different sources, and have a simple system for organising and planning your posts.

Most importantly, you should be able to answer three questions:

- What should I create?
- Where can I find ideas?
- How will I organise my content and publish consistently?

Your personal brand grows through what people repeatedly see, learn, and experience from you.

Build a strategy that gives your content direction, develop a habit of finding ideas, and establish a system that helps you keep showing up.

Don't just post more. Start posting with purpose.
